title: PixelDiT2: Representation-Grounded Pixel Diffusion Transformers
claim: A frozen pretrained encoder supplies per-patch guidance to the generator, giving high-quality samples and much faster convergence than the baseline.
layout: Top 2x5 photo gallery; bottom-left diagram, bottom-right line plot
description: The figure has three parts. The top two rows are a 2x5 grid of high-quality class-conditional ImageNet samples: a red panda, an espresso cup, a dog, a volcano, a bottle cap, a soup pot, a squirrel, a car mirror, a lemur and a child in a knit hat. The bottom left is a teal block diagram. A ViT Encoder feeds a DiT Projection block, which also takes a timestep embedding. The projection outputs a Grounding Token, which modulates the DiT Blocks (repeated xN) through Spatial AdaLN. A Noisy Image enters through patchify, and a class embedding is also fed in. The bottom right is a line plot of FID-50K against training epoch. The teal PixelDiT2 curve sits well below the dashed gray PixelDiT curve and ends at 1.48. The eye goes first to the photo gallery.
caption: \textbf{\model{} at ImageNet-$512{\times}512$: samples, architecture, and convergence.} Top two rows: Class-conditional samples spanning diverse subjects, compositions, and textures. Bottom left: The noisy image follows the pixel-denoising path. In parallel, a frozen vision encoder produces per-patch features; the timestep-conditioned DiT block $P_g$ maps them to \scaffold that modulate the diffusion transformer through spatial AdaLN [ref]. Bottom right: \model{} reaches FID $1.78$ at epoch $200$ and $1.48$ at epoch $680$. \model{} surpasses PixelDiT's 850-epoch FID by epoch $200$, a $4.25\times$ lower epoch budget.
abstract: Recent advances in pixel-space diffusion models have narrowed the image quality gap with latent-space diffusion, but still converge more slowly and lag behind in final image quality. We argue that a key reason is the lack of an explicit representation prior: unlike latent diffusion, which usually denoises in a compact and structured latent space, pixel diffusion needs to learn denoising-friendly representations and pixel generation simultaneously from raw RGB space. To address this problem, we propose PixelDiT2, an end-to-end pixel-space diffusion model designed to decouple representation learning from pixel generation without introducing an autoencoder or latent reconstruction bottleneck. We propose representation grounding that uses a frozen pretrained vision foundation model to provide explicit per-patch representation guidance throughout denoising, allowing the pixel diffusion transformer to focus more on pixel generation. On ImageNet-256x256, PixelDiT2 achieves an FID of 1.46 after 600 epochs; at 512x512 resolution, PixelDiT2 achieves an FID of 1.48 after 680 epochs. Project page: https://pixeldit.github.io/pixeldit2/
